item.text: {"question_id":"6B.9","answer":"During 2023, Lula’s administration created or restored several formally authorized institutions, including the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples, Funai’s restructuring, Indigenous Policy Council, LGBTQI+ Rights Council, vaccination-coordination unit, and Novo PAC’s interministerial committees (BATCH-0001-E036; BATCH-0001-E037; BATCH-0016-E015; BATCH-0018-E006). The Bolsa Família framework added statutory integration with SUAS, decentralized management, public beneficiary information, social-control councils, a federal inspection network, performance-linked subnational funding, and CadÚnico interoperability (BATCH-0019-E001; BATCH-0019-E003; BATCH-0019-E005). These designs were accompanied by enacted 2023 credits for Bolsa Família, health, and other ministries, and by budget recomposition in selected environmental and climate-policy areas (BATCH-0020-E006; BATCH-0007-E011; BATCH-0007-E012). However, the evidence does not establish reliable recurring funding, professional staffing, transparent operational standards, or resilience beyond personal rule. Several bodies lacked demonstrated activity or results: only eight of seventeen mapped environmental councils were active, the sanitation interministerial committee was inoperative, and audits found monitoring, data, control, and policy-design weaknesses (BATCH-0007-E011; BATCH-0005-E003; BATCH-0005-E008). Yanomami deployment and housing delivery demonstrate short-period implementation or outputs, but not institutional durability (BATCH-0013-E004; BATCH-0016-E013). The 2023 record therefore supports institutional construction and some implementation capacity, while leaving long-term durability and post-Lula resilience unresolved.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E036","BATCH-0001-E037","BATCH-0016-E015","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0019-E003","BATCH-0019-E005","BATCH-0020-E006","BATCH-0007-E011","BATCH-0007-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0007-E011","BATCH-0005-E003","BATCH-0005-E008","BATCH-0013-E004","BATCH-0016-E013","BATCH-0020-E003","BATCH-0020-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The one-year 2023 period cannot establish resilience beyond Lula’s rule.","Enacted budget credits and selected budget increases do not establish execution, recurring financing, staffing continuity, or outcomes.","The supplied evidence does not adequately document professional staffing or transparent standards across the institutions.","The PPA 2024–2027 and Monitora targets are forward commitments and are not used as evidence of demonstrated 2023 durability (BATCH-0017-E002; BATCH-0017-E003; BATCH-0020-E003; BATCH-0020-E004).","Attribution is generally to Lula’s federal administration or ministries; several measures also depended on Congress, subnational governments, or institutional procedures."],"corrections_made":["Removed unsupported claims that institutional creation, budget authorization, or short-term deployment demonstrated durable funding, professional staffing, transparent standards, or resilience.","Removed the post-2023 PPA as evidence of 2023 durability.","Retained statutory design, enacted resources, and documented implementation as material but limited support.","Added the environmental-council inactivity, sanitation-coordination failure, and audit findings as direct qualifications.","Preserved the distinction between institutional creation, short-term outputs, and demonstrated durability."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Evidence of multi-year budget execution, staffing and retention, operational standards, independent evaluations, and institutional continuity after Lula’s period would materially change the durability assessment.","The current supplied record does not resolve whether the newly created or restored institutions became resilient beyond presidential or coalition changes."]}
